newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PLAYERS' UNION TO HOLD CHARITY MATCH FOR BOSMAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLAYERS' UNION TO HOLD CHARITY MATCH FOR BOSMAN.

text.p: A soccer players' union launched last year by Diego Maradona and Eric Cantona said on Monday it would hold a charity match for Belgium's Jean-Marc Bosman next April.

At a meeting in Paris, which Maradona and Cantona did not attend, the International Association of Professionnal Footballers (AIFP) also said it would open a bank account for donations to Bosman, the player who earned the right for his European colleagues to work freely inside the European Union.

"We had to show our solidarity towards a man who launched a revolution within soccer," said French international goalkeeper Bernard Lama, who chaired the meeting. "Thanks to him things have changed at last in our circles."
The match will be played on April 1. Lama was unable to say who would play and where it would be held.
Bosman said: "I thank all the players because for a long time I was fighting on my own and it's a good reward to feel supported by some of the leading names in the game."
A committee was also created to try to find ways to finance the union, which until now has been funded by its members.
One year after its creation, the AIFP has remained very low-profile but Lama said it aimed to become "a new partner in discussions with international bodies".
Italy's Gianluca Vialli said the union had learnt from mistakes in the past year and would be more active this year.

Among others, Arsenal's French coach Arsene Wenger, Brazilians Rai and Valdo, French internationals Franck Leboeuf, Vincent Guerin and Eric Di Meco and former Argentine international Jorge Valdano attended the meeting.
Vialli said Cantona and Maradona were unable to attend because of professional and family commitments.
